newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stock index up over two percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stock index up over two percent.

text.p: Jakarta stocks surged further in mid-afternoon trade on Thursday, taking the composite index to 686.21 points, up 2.1 percent.
Brokers attributed the sharp rise to widespread buying of blue-chips, including Telkom and Citra Marga.

"Telkom rose sharply on intense market talk that it will do a private placement after previous rumours that Singapore Telecom had bought a stake in the firm," said one broker with a Singapore-based firm.
The broker said that although a Telkom official had said the company has no plans to sell a stake to Singapore Telecom, both foreign and domestic investors kept buying the stock.
Telkom was last at 4,075 rupiah, up 175, on a volume of 3.4 million shares.
Sustained buying interest was also seen on toll road operator Citra Marga on market talk that its net profit in the first quarter was up, brokers said.
"It is also linked to rumours that Citra Marga will propose a rights issue," one broker said.
Citra Marga rose 125 rupiah to 2,350 rupiah on a volume of 5.3 million shares.
Buying was also seen on other blue chip counters such as Bank Negara Indonesia, noodle maker Indofood and cigarette maker Sampoerna, brokers said.
